[quote=technokratisches_kaiserreich;59990275][spoiler=[b]Skies and Seas[/b]]

The chaff spraying missiles launched by the air defense systems before they were swiftly destroyed would have little effect on the SM-6s. The SM-6 missiles traveling at hypersonic speeds would be extremely hard to intercept as they rocket toward the retreating enemy aircraft. Datalink would allow the missiles to bypass chaff as radars from a wide variety of systems: aircraft, ships and others would allow the missile to continue to be accurate. The SM-6s would likely cause significant damage to the retreating aircraft, their speed far outpacing that of the aircraft. 

Grounding the aircraft would prove to be a blunder. No longer mobile, the aircraft proved to be a target for long-range cruise missile strikes. 90 Donnerkeil cruise missiles are dispatched to the runways and air bases where the aircraft are parked to destroy them along with aviation fuel. 

Drones would be largely ineffective. Large swarm tactics werent utilized by the loitering munitions. The large number of drones would quickly disperse, stay low to avoid detection and would lack on emissions to avoid other drones finding them. Their stealth and quick execution would make them deadly especially as they go after the anti-air systems in the south. A total of five drones are taken out by the swarm but most of them continue to move towards the anti-air. 

As the drones approached the J-16CJ strike groups the ships would use their THOR systems to destroy them in the sky. High powered microwaves would slam into the swarm frying its electronics and forcing them to fall out of the sky. 

Again the activation of even more air defense would paint another target for the Reichswehr. The J-16CJ strike groups would slam their REG-3000 missiles, salvo after salvo towards the southern air defenses. The aim would be to pair those missiles with drones to ensure their destruction. 

The submarines would inflict limited damage on the fleet. Anti-submarine aircraft, deploying sonobuoys would allow the fleet to detect the submarines 100 km outuncomfortably close but manageable. Using a mix of passive and active detection the movements and locations of the submarines would be parsed together. 

LANCELOT-AR missiles would be deployed again. These hypersonic missiles would have a far longer range than torpedoes. Once it gets close to the subs they would drop their torpedo payloads which hone onto the subs. ASW helicopters using magnetic anomaly detectors would pick up on the subs as well and fire their own LANCELOT-AR payloads. 

However, the defenses, although significant, wouldn't prove invincible. The MS Eisenfels cargo ship would be sunk by a torpedo attack along with damage to a patrol corvette.[/spoiler]

The navy had been pushed back and heavily damaged by combined losses in their own waters and in Nestorstaat. Only southern air defenses remained in Hydronia and even those being pummeled by REG-3000s. The Kaiserreich now held de facto air and naval superiority in the area. 

Now was the perfect time to land the Marineinfantriekorps in eastern Hydronia. When the coastal defences of Hydronia were heavily damaged the amphibious assault ships moved within 20-50 km of the beachhead while the fleet provided air defence. Massive naval gunfire would be used to suppress any resistance with Hydronian troops in the north, uncovered by air defenses being pummeled by Donnerkeil cruise missile strikes along with JDAMs. 

LCACs would move to bring tanks, armored vehicles and supplies as a combination of helicopters and LCAC would move troops into the area. Paratroopers ahead of time would jump into enemy territory to sabotage enemy reinforcements and force the enemy to fight both the beachhead and their rear.[/spoiler]
